parts.title: Word List
parts.content:
Detailed Meanings

😎
advocate[ædvəkeit]v.
To advocate a plan or idea is to support or suggest it in public.
→ The group advocated increased spending on education and schools.
😎
authorize[ɔ:θəraiz]v.
To authorize something means to give permission for it.
→ The mayor authorized the construction of a new statue in the park.
😎
civilian[siviljən]n.
A civilian is someone who is not in the military.
→ It was Todd’s job to keep civilians from entering the army facility.
😎
commodity[kəmɔdəti]n.
A commodity is something that can be bought or sold.
→ Fran’s uncle made most of his money trading commodities.
😎
conquest[kɔŋkwest]n.
A conquest is an event by which one country takes over another country.
→ After the conquest, the people of the small city had no freedom.
😎
disclose[disklouz]v.
To disclose something means to tell it to someone else.
→ John came home late, so he had to disclose his activities to his wife.
😎
dynamics[dainæmiks]n.
The dynamics of a situation are the way that parts of it affect each other.
→ A good psychologist needs to know a lot about the dynamics of brain disorders.
😎
enroll[enroul]v.
To enroll in something is to put one’s name on a list as a member of a group.
→ The students had to enroll in the class one semester in advance.
😎
envious[enviəs]adj.
When someone is envious, they want something that another person has.
→ They were envious of their neighbor’s front yard.
😎
euphoria[ju:fɔ:riə]n.
Euphoria is a feeling of extreme happiness.
→ The athlete felt euphoria after he won the important game.
😎
festive[festiv]adj.
When something is festive, it is happy and related to a party or celebration.
→ Dean’s favorite part of Christmas is the festive clothing that people wear.
😎
jolly[dʒɔli]adj.
When someone is jolly, they are cheerful and happy.
→ My grandmother’s jolly attitude always made me smile.
😎
lentil[lentil]n.
Lentils are very small beans that people cook and eat.
→ Danni made her special soup with lentils when her husband was sick.
😎
marshal[mɑ:rʃəl]v.
To marshal a group means to assemble them in order.
→ The students were marshaled outside and put into groups.
😎
morale[məral]n.
Morale is the amount of hope that people have during a difficult situation.
→ To improve our family’s morale, mom suggested going on a picnic.
😎
prophecy[prɔfəsi]n.
A prophecy is a prediction about what will happen in the future.
→ Some people believe that prophecies are actually true.
😎
sage[seidʒ]n.
A sage is someone who is very wise.
→ Hal always visited the local sage for help with love.
😎
senate[senət]n.
A senate is a part of the government in some countries.
→ Everybody liked Caroline and chose her to speak for them in the senate.
😎
sentiment[sentəmənt]n.
A sentiment is an opinion based on your feelings.
→ Tess told everyone at the table her sentiments about eating meat.
😎
unrest[ʌnrest]n.
Unrest is a state of anger about something among the people in a place.
→ High taxes caused much of the unrest that led to the Revolutionary War.

sections.title: Exercise 1: Choose the answer that best fits the question.

questions.content: Who is a person with the power to authorize a war?
questions.explanation: A president has the power to authorize a war.

questions.content: Which of the following might give you euphoria?
questions.explanation: Winning a great prize can give you euphoria.
A sage is very wise or intelligent.

questions.content: Which of the following is a valuable commodity?
questions.explanation: Oil is a valuable commodity.

questions.content: What might cause unrest at a school?
options: Students getting rewarded for good grades
Students being told to go home early
questions.explanation: Students having daily tests might cause unrest.

sections.title: Exercise 2: Choose the one that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

questions.explanation: The opposite of authorize is reject.
The opposite of conquest is liberation.
The opposite of disclose is conceal.
The opposite of euphoria is depression.
The opposite of unrest is peace.
The opposite of sage is fool.
The opposite of civilian is soldier.
The opposite of festive is unhappy.
The opposite of enroll is quit.
The opposite of advocate is oppose.

sections.title: Exercise 3: Choose the one that is similar in meaning to the given word.

questions.explanation: A lentil is similar to a bean.
Envious is similar to jealous.
A commodity is similar to a product.
Dynamics is similar to aspects.
A prophecy is similar to a prediction.
Morale is similar to confidence.
To marshal is similar to assemble.
Jolly is similar to merry.
A senate is similar to a government.
Sentiment is similar to opinion.

sections.title: Exercise 4: Write C if the italicized word is used correctly. Write I if the word is used incorrectly.

questions.content: Janice’s dad was a part of the senate. He fixed cars all day.
questions.explanation: Senate is a part of government, not related to fixing cars.

questions.content: Damon read about the Roman conquest of northern Africa. He was amazed by all the places that the Romans took over.
questions.explanation: Conquest means taking over another country.

questions.content: The teacher understood the dynamics between instructors and students in the classroom.
questions.explanation: Dynamics means the way that parts of a situation affect each other.

questions.content: Mariah enrolled the clothes and put them in her drawer.
questions.explanation: Enroll means to put one's name on a list, not related to clothes.

questions.content: Sheldon was a vegetarian. He advocated for people not to eat meat.
questions.explanation: Advocate means to support or suggest an idea in public.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
The Lydian King

King Croesus was once one of the richest kings in the world. He ruled over Lydia, an ancient empire located near modern-day Turkey and controlled a valuable commodity: gold. Many people were very envious of him.

One day, a messenger disclosed some interesting news: political unrest in Persia had weakened the empire. Before then, the Persians had taken over many countries. Many leaders were scared of the Persian conquest. But King Croesus understood the dynamics of war better than most. He decided that it would be a good time to try to beat the Persians while they were weak.

He advocated starting war, but nobody shared his sentiment. Then he asked a wise member of the senate who was visiting from Athens. The sage didn’t say whether he should attack the Persians or not. He only warned him that his good luck wouldn’t last.

Finally, King Croesus sent a messenger to visit the Oracle, a special lady who could see the future. The messenger gave the Oracle jugs of wine and baskets of lentils in order to make her happy.

When the messenger came back, he was in a festive mood.

“What was the Oracle’s prophecy?” asked King Croesus.

The jolly messenger responded, “She said that if you attack Persia, you will destroy a great empire.”

The news filled Croesus with euphoria. After hearing the Oracle’s prophecy, many civilians enrolled in the Lydian army. The king marshaled his troops and prepared them for a war with Persia. Their morale was high because they were sure they would win. Soon, King Croesus authorized an attack against the Persians.

However, the Persian army was still very strong. After a few months of fighting, it was obvious that the Oracle’s prophecy had come true: by attacking the Persians, King Croesus had destroyed a great empire—his own! King Croesus should have considered the advice more carefully.

sections.title: Part A: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: People were envious of King Croesus because he understood the dynamics of war better than anybody else.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Sai (F). Mọi người ghen tị với Vua Croesus vì ông kiểm soát một mặt hàng có giá trị là vàng: "...controlled a valuable commodity: gold. Many people were very envious of him" (...kiểm soát một mặt hàng có giá trị: vàng. Nhiều người rất ghen tị với ông). Chứ không phải vì ông hiểu về động lực chiến tranh.

questions.content: The messenger disclosed that the Persians were in a state of unrest.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Đúng (T). Ngay đầu đoạn hai, bài đọc cho biết: "One day, a messenger disclosed some interesting news: political unrest in Persia had weakened the empire" (Một ngày nọ, một sứ giả tiết lộ tin tức thú vị: tình trạng bất ổn chính trị ở Ba Tư đã làm suy yếu đế chế).

questions.content: The sage man from the senate was the only one that shared the king’s sentiment.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Sai (F). Vị hiền triết (sage) không hề chia sẻ quan điểm với nhà vua, mà chỉ cảnh báo ông rằng sự may mắn của ông sẽ không kéo dài mãi: "The sage didn’t say whether he should attack the Persians or not. He only warned him that his good luck wouldn’t last."

questions.content: The messenger gave the Oracle jugs of wine and baskets of lentils to make her happy.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Đúng (T). Trong đoạn bốn có viết rõ chi tiết này: "The messenger gave the Oracle jugs of wine and baskets of lentils in order to make her happy" (Sứ giả đã tặng Oracle những bình rượu và giỏ đậu lăng để làm bà vui).

questions.content: The Oracle’s prophecy was that the Lydian conquest of Persia would be successful.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Sai (F). Lời tiên tri không nói là Lydia sẽ chiến thắng, mà chỉ dự báo rằng: "She said that if you attack Persia, you will destroy a great empire" (Bà ấy nói rằng nếu ngài tấn công Ba Tư, ngài sẽ tiêu diệt một đế chế vĩ đại). Và hóa ra "đế chế vĩ đại" bị tiêu diệt lại chính là vương quốc của ông.

questions.content: Why did King Croesus advocate war against the Persians?
options: He wanted to take their gold.
King Croesus advocated war with the Persians because the Persians were politically weak.
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là A. Ở đoạn hai, tác giả viết: "He decided that it would be a good time to try to beat the Persians while they were weak" (Ông quyết định rằng đây sẽ là thời điểm tốt để đánh bại người Ba Tư trong khi họ đang suy yếu).

questions.content: Why was the messenger in a festive and jolly mood when he returned from seeing the Oracle?
options: The messenger was in a festive and jolly mood because he thought the Oracle’s prophecy was good for the Lydians.
Because he drank all the wine.
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là A. Người sứ giả rất vui vẻ vì anh ta tin rằng lời tiên tri của Oracle là một dự báo tốt đẹp cho quân đội Lydia (nghĩ rằng đế chế Ba Tư sẽ bị tiêu diệt). Sự vui mừng này được thể hiện qua các từ "festive mood" và "jolly".

questions.content: How did King Croesus feel after he heard the Oracle’s prophecy?
options: King Croesus was filled with euphoria after he heard the Oracle’s prophecy.
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là A. Ngay đầu đoạn tám, bài viết miêu tả cảm xúc của nhà vua: "The news filled Croesus with euphoria" (Tin tức khiến Croesus tràn ngập cảm giác sung sướng tột độ).

questions.content: How did the civilians who enrolled and were marshaled in the Lydian army feel about the war?
options: They had low morale and wanted to quit.
They were scared of the Persians.
The civilians who enrolled and were marshaled in the army had high morale because they thought they would win.
They were envious of the king.
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là A. Ở đoạn tám miêu tả tâm trạng của binh lính và dân thường tham gia quân đội: "Their morale was high because they were sure they would win" (Tinh thần của họ rất cao vì họ chắc chắn rằng mình sẽ chiến thắng).

questions.content: What did King Croesus learn from the experience?
options: He learned how to fight better.
He learned that the Oracle lied.
He learned that Persians are friendly.
King Croesus learned that he should have considered advice more carefully.
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là A. Câu cuối cùng của câu chuyện đúc kết lại bài học mà ông nhận được: "King Croesus should have considered the advice more carefully" (Vua Croesus lẽ ra nên cân nhắc lời khuyên một cách cẩn thận hơn).

parts.translation:
Vị vua nước Lydia

Vua Croesus từng là một trong những vị vua giàu có nhất thế giới. Ông cai trị Lydia, một đế chế cổ đại nằm gần Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ ngày nay và kiểm soát một hàng hoá có giá trị: vàng. Nhiều người rất ghen tị với ông.

Một ngày nọ, một sứ giả tiết lộ một số tin tức thú vị: sự bất ổn chính trị ở Ba Tư đã làm suy yếu đế chế này. Trước đó, người Ba Tư đã chiếm lấy nhiều quốc gia. Nhiều nhà lãnh đạo sợ hãi sự chinh phục của Ba Tư. Nhưng Vua Croesus hiểu rõ động lực của chiến tranh hơn hầu hết mọi người. Ông quyết định rằng đây sẽ là thời điểm tốt để cố gắng đánh bại người Ba Tư trong khi họ đang suy yếu.

Ông ủng hộ việc bắt đầu chiến tranh, nhưng không ai chia sẻ quan điểm của ông. Sau đó, ông đã hỏi một thành viên thông thái của thượng viện đang đến thăm từ Athens. Vị hiền triết không nói liệu ông có nên tấn công người Ba Tư hay không. Ông ấy chỉ cảnh báo ông rằng sự may mắn của ông sẽ không kéo dài.

Cuối cùng, Vua Croesus cử một sứ giả đến thăm Nhà tiên tri Oracle, một người phụ nữ đặc biệt có thể nhìn thấy tương lai. Người sứ giả đã đưa cho Oracle những bình rượu và những giỏ đậu lăng để làm bà vui vẻ.

Khi sứ giả trở về, anh ta đang trong một tâm trạng hân hoan.

"Lời tiên tri của Oracle là gì?" Vua Croesus hỏi.

Người sứ giả vui vẻ trả lời: "Bà ấy nói rằng nếu ngài tấn công Ba Tư, ngài sẽ phá huỷ một đế chế vĩ đại."

Tin tức này khiến Croesus tràn ngập sự hưng phấn. Sau khi nghe lời tiên tri của Oracle, nhiều dân thường đã đăng ký vào quân đội Lydia. Nhà vua đã tập hợp quân đội của mình và chuẩn bị cho họ một cuộc chiến với Ba Tư. Tinh thần của họ rất cao vì họ chắc chắn rằng mình sẽ chiến thắng. Chẳng bao lâu, Vua Croesus đã cho phép một cuộc tấn công chống lại người Ba Tư.

Tuy nhiên, quân đội Ba Tư vẫn rất mạnh. Sau một vài tháng chiến đấu, rõ ràng là lời tiên tri của Oracle đã trở thành sự thật: bằng cách tấn công người Ba Tư, Vua Croesus đã phá huỷ một đế chế vĩ đại — đế chế của chính mình! Vua Croesus đáng lẽ nên xem xét lời khuyên một cách cẩn thận hơn.
